class.slave.family.JPN: into a family of bonded servants
class.noble.family.JPN: into a house of court nobles or lords
prof.farmer.desc.JPN: Paddy fields, barley on the dry plots and the lord's tax paid in rice.
prof.laborer.desc.JPN: Carrying, digging, hauling boats – any work for a handful of coins or rice.
prof.artisan.desc.JPN: Carpenter, potter, lacquerer or papermaker: the craft passes from father to son.
prof.weaver.desc.JPN: You spin ramie and silk and weave cloth for the tax and for sale.
prof.midwife.desc.JPN: You help at births and know herbs and charms against evil spirits.
prof.merchant.desc.JPN: Rice, salt, silk and copper coins: buy at one market, sell at another. Trading is hard without a guild.
prof.sailor.desc.JPN: Nets, oars and cargo carried along the coast. The sea feeds you, and the sea takes.
prof.soldier.desc.JPN: A foot soldier with no land of his own: a spear, later a gun, pay and plunder. You go where your lord sends you.
prof.scribe.desc.JPN: Deeds, land registers and lords' letters. Few can handle brush and ink.
prof.physician.desc.JPN: You heal by the kanpō books: pulse reading, needles, moxa and remedies made from roots.
prof.priest.desc.JPN: A shaved head, sutras, vows. A Buddhist monastery is a school, a bank and sometimes a fortress.
prof.landholder.desc.JPN: You collect the villages' tax, judge peasants and send warriors when your lord calls.
prof.magistrate.desc.JPN: A shugo or a lord's counsellor: power over a whole province, and with it envy and plots.
prof.matron.as.JPN: the lady of a great house
prof.matron.desc.JPN: You run a great household: servants, storehouses, taxes and, with your husband away, its defence.
prof.household_slave.desc.JPN: A genin in the master's house: kitchen, water, errands. You can be sold or passed on as an inheritance.
prof.field_slave.desc.JPN: You work the master's fields with no land of your own and no right to leave.
prof.officer.desc.JPN: You lead a band of spearmen or gunners and answer to your lord for every one of them.
prof.workshop_owner.desc.JPN: Your own workshop, apprentices and a seat in the za guild.
prof.shipowner.desc.JPN: Your ships sail to China, Korea and across the Inland Sea.
prof.official.desc.JPN: Service in the office of the shogunate or a lord: lawsuits, registers, seals.
prof.overseer.desc.JPN: A genin whom the master trusts with the household and the other servants.
prof.samurai.desc: You serve your lord with sword and bow, and later the gun. Loyalty brings land and honour; failure brings death or disgrace.
prof.shrine_priest.desc: You serve the kami at a Shinto shrine: purifications, festivals, prayers for the harvest.
prof.swordsmith.desc: You fold and hammer the steel hundreds of times. One good blade can make your name last for centuries.
prof.sake_brewer.desc: You brew rice sake. Brewers grow rich and often lend money at interest.
prof.noh_actor.desc: A mask, a slow dance, chanting to flute and drums. Troupes seek the patronage of nobles and temples.
prof.ama_diver.desc: You dive without any gear for abalone and seaweed. Cold and dangerous, but it pays in hard coin.
prof.tea_master.desc: You host tea gatherings and know bowls and scrolls. Even lords listen to a tea connoisseur.
focus.learn.desc.JPN: A temple monk teaches kana and counting. The family pays
focus.study.desc.JPN: Books of the sages, calligraphy, waka poems. Costs money
focus.health.desc.JPN: Hot springs, baths, rest and herbs
focus.religion.desc.JPN: Sutras, offerings to the kami, pilgrimages
lifestyle.food.plain.desc.JPN: Rice with millet, miso soup, pickles, sometimes fish
lifestyle.food.varied.desc.JPN: White rice, fish, tofu, vegetables and fruit. Good for health
lifestyle.food.feasts.desc.JPN: Banquets with sake, guests and a dozen dishes. Expensive
lifestyle.exercise.gymnasium.desc.JPN: Bow, sword, riding, sumo wrestling. Stronger and healthier
lifestyle.medicine.temple.desc.JPN: Yakushi the Medicine Buddha and charms from the shrine
lifestyle.medicine.physician.desc.JPN: A kanpō physician with herbs and needles looks after the family. Expensive
lifestyle.baths.rarely.desc.JPN: The river and a tub at home
lifestyle.baths.sometimes.desc.JPN: The temple bath on days it opens to everyone
lifestyle.baths.daily.desc.JPN: A town steam bath: warmth, talk, news. Must live in a town
religion.buddhist.kyoto: the Buddhism of the capital's temples
ev.d_m_grave.text.JPN: You brought rice, sake and flowers to the grave stone, lit a stick of incense and told them everything that had happened this year. The wind rustled the bamboo, as if someone were listening.
ev.w_tomb_visit.text.JPN: In the days of Bon you washed the family stones, set out rice, sake and flowers and spoke the names of the dead aloud, so the souls would know they are remembered and awaited.
ev.w_old_sun_bench.text.JPN: A warm veranda, sunshine, a cup of warmed sake and nothing to do until evening. You never knew life could be like this.
ev.w_old_storyteller.text.JPN: The young ones at the gate don't believe that rice cost half as much when you were young and that winter snow lay higher than the roofs. You tell them anyway – and every time the drifts get deeper.
ev.j_hs_secret.text.JPN: Pouring sake, you overheard the master talking with a guest about a deal nobody was supposed to know about. Next morning at the market a man from his rival came up and offered you a string of coins for the details.
ev.j_ovs_will.text.JPN: After a few cups of sake the master promises: if the household prospers, he will set you free. It isn't the first time he's said so.
ev.j_fs_rations.text.JPN: The steward has cut the rice ration again and sells the surplus on the side. Tomorrow the lord himself comes to the estate, for the first time in a year.
ev.t_grain_hoard.text.JPN: The harvest has failed, the merchants' rice boats aren't coming, and prices have tripled. Your storehouses, though, are full. At the gate stand dealers with strings of coins and hungry people with empty baskets.
ev.j_ship_state.text.JPN: The lord needs boats to carry the rice tax to the capital. Those who carry his cargo are promised fixed pay and protection. A private run might earn twice as much – or nothing.
ev.j_pri_omen.text.JPN: Before a great undertaking the lord ordered a divination. You read the cracks in the tortoise shell: the signs are bad, as bad as they come. And the man who ordered it looks at you, waiting for one answer only.
ev.a_inheritance.text.JPN: The inheritance isn't even divided yet, and {npc} already wants the best rice field whole: "I'm the one who looked after the old man while you were off who knows where." And {g=npc_sex:he|she} has a point.
ev.a_inheritance.court.success.JPN: The court gave you more than half. You got the field and lost your family.
